Believe that life _is_ worth living, and your belief will help create the fact.” Exact match apart from the italic on “is”, which the card cannot carry and the note already discloses. The paragraph continues with the scientific proof sentence and closes with the Henry IV and Crillon anecdote at lines 2225 to 2227, so “final paragraph”, not closing sentence, is the correct locator and the note says so. Attribution sound; the line is James’s own, no speaker. Original English, 1897, in scope. One borderline worth recording: the piece began as an 1895 address to the Harvard YMCA (Gutenberg footnote 1), but James published it in a book subtitled Essays in Popular Philosophy and the citation is to that printed text, so Essay is the right tag and the oratory exclusion does not bite. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, 0 of 3, not banned.
